recognize_zh: 幾乎所有紅血球表面都有不規則的淡染缺損、像被蟲蛀的「凹洞」（pitted surface），邊緣呈扇貝狀或不規則，這是冷沉球蛋白（cryoglobulin）沉積在紅血球上造成的人工假象，而不是真正的紅血球異形。
features: Nearly all red cells show irregular pale, punched-out or moth-eaten areas on their surface
Irregular, scalloped red cell outlines without true spicules
No discrete basophilic inclusions or parasites within the pale areas
Occasional small platelets; one large pale finely granular structure (possible precipitate or degenerated cell)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a diffuse, uniform artifact in which almost all red cells display irregular pale pitted or moth-eaten surface defects with scalloped outlines. No intraerythrocytic parasites, basophilic stippling or discrete inclusions are identified within the defects. Similar changes affecting virtually every red cell point to a preparation-related rather than intrinsic red cell abnormality. In a patient with type 1 cryoglobulinemia, findings are consistent with cryoglobulin precipitate artifact; preparing a smear from a pre-warmed (37 C) sample is recommended to confirm.

ddx.vs: Water artifact produces refractile, sharply outlined bubbles that shift with focus and is not linked to cold, whereas cryoglobulin artifact resolves on warming the sample.
Echinocytes have regular, evenly spaced short projections around the circumference rather than irregular pale pits across the cell surface.
Parasites show discrete chromatin dots with cytoplasm (rings), whereas these pale defects lack chromatin or defined structure.
Acanthocytes are dense spheroidal cells with few irregular long spicules and no central pitting.
